questions.title: Draw a House Using Canvas API
questions.content: Create an HTML page that uses Canvas API to draw a simple house using rectangles and triangles.

examples.explanation: Canvas can draw complex graphics using shapes.

solutions.title: Canvas House
solutions.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>House</title>
</head>
<body>
    <canvas id="c" width="300" height="200"></canvas>

    <script>
        const ctx = document.getElementById('c').getContext('2d');

        ctx.fillStyle = 'brown';
        ctx.fillRect(100, 100, 100, 80);

        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.moveTo(100, 100);
        ctx.lineTo(150, 50);
        ctx.lineTo(200, 100);
        ctx.fillStyle = 'red';
        ctx.fill();
    </script>
</body>
</html>

questions.title: Build a Drawing App Using Canvas
questions.content: Create a simple drawing app using Canvas where the user can draw freehand using mouse events.

examples.explanation: Canvas supports interactive drawing.

solutions.title: Canvas Drawing App
solutions.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Drawing App</title>
</head>
<body>
    <canvas id="draw" width="400" height="300" style="border:1px solid black"></canvas>

    <script>
        const canvas = document.getElementById('draw');
        const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
        let drawing = false;

        canvas.onmousedown = () => drawing = true;
        canvas.onmouseup = () => drawing = false;
        canvas.onmousemove = (e) => {
            if (!drawing) return;
            ctx.fillStyle = 'black';
            ctx.fillRect(e.offsetX, e.offsetY, 2, 2);
        };
    </script>
</body>
</html>

questions.title: Build a Canvas-Based Game Board
questions.content: Create a simple grid-based game board using Canvas and demonstrate difference from SVG rendering.

examples.explanation: Canvas is suitable for game rendering.

solutions.title: Canvas Grid Board
solutions.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Grid Board</title>
</head>
<body>
    <canvas id="grid" width="300" height="300"></canvas>

    <script>
        const ctx = document.getElementById('grid').getContext('2d');
        for (let i = 0; i <= 300; i += 30) {
            ctx.moveTo(i, 0);
            ctx.lineTo(i, 300);
            ctx.moveTo(0, i);
            ctx.lineTo(300, i);
        }
        ctx.stroke();
    </script>
</body>
</html>
